question.text: If the number of ways in which four distinct balls can be put into two identical boxes such that no box remains empty is equal to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>k</mi></math>, then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>k</mi></math> is

solution.text:
Every ball has two options

⇒   4  balls can be put in 24 ways.

Arrangement among themselves is 2!

So, total ways=12!×24= 23

But, above count also includes the one case in which all the balls are put in one box,

⇒  required number of ways  k= 23-1=7
